name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: Early US flu season; no system strain found
summary: US flu admissions rose 38% to 8,396 in the week to 31 Oct, early for the season; UK flu above baseline
state: CDC data for the week to 31 Oct showed 8,396 flu admissions, up 38% on the week and higher than usual for the time of year, though severity was rated low; H1N1 made up 97.7% of subtyped flu A (Medical Daily, 9 Nov). UKHSA's report of 5 Nov shows flu activity above baseline with admissions in the low-impact range (UKHSA). Searches on 16 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so an early US season keeps Watch.
for_you: The NHS offers free flu vaccination to over-65s, pregnant women, young children and people with some health conditions; UKHSA advises staying home when unwell.
rubric_hit: Unusually early US flu season (8,396 admissions, week to 31 Oct) meets Watch; no variant of concern or system strain

sources.title: Medical Daily — Flu hospital admissions rose 38% to 8,396 in one week as CDC forecasts further increases
UKHSA — National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 5 November 2026 (week 45)

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
